title: SDK integration bundles: reference snippets for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and CLI
creator: Asha Patel
description: Bundle a set of small, opinionated reference integrations across TS/Python/Go that demonstrate production patterns for retries, backoff, streaming ergonomics, and minimal deployment setups. Deliver four focused reference apps: (1) Next.js route using server and edge runtimes with streaming/SSR example and client-side hydration; (2) FastAPI async service showing SSE and background KV cache usage; (3) Go net/http server demonstrating efficient goroutine-based streaming, per-request context cancellation, and connection reuse; (4) CLI examples (ts-node and python click) showing retry wrappers, idempotent request design, and chunked streaming output. The goal is a low-friction onboarding surface engineers can clone and run locally or in a simple Cloud Run/GCP/AWS container. This ticket covers implementation + minimal docs + 1 integration test per language. Acceptance criteria: runnable repos locally, CI lint and basic integration test, one-page README for each app with deploy notes and retry/timeout guidelines, and a single PR that links to the SDK package and publishing instructions.
updates: 2026-02-20 — Created ticket. Initial scope drafted after cross-functional sync with DX and Docs. Decision: keep bundles lightweight (<=200 LOC per example) and prefer explicit patterns over magic helpers.

2026-02-25 — Spike: evaluated streaming patterns in TS and Go. Trade-off: fetch-based streaming on the edge has payload size limits; opting for hybrid approach in Next.js with server-sent events fallback for long-lived streams. Notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Integration+Bundles

2026-03-01 — Prototype commits: added FastAPI SSE example and Python CLI using click. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/234. Early feedback from PM (Miguel Herrera): surface recommended timeouts and tokenization cost estimate in the README.

2026-03-04 — Design review: agreed on consistent retry semantics across languages: exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 4, idempotency key guidance for non-idempotent ops. Design notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SDK-integration-guidelines (internal).

2026-03-07 — Security review request queued. Security asked for explicit guidance on KMS usage for private deploy snippets; marked security_review_required=false for this ticket but will add guidance links to the Private deployment playbook.
notes: Implementation details: Next.js example exports two routes: /api/stream (server runtime) and /edge/stream (edge runtime) with identical SDK call signatures and a tiny adapter layer. Demonstrates streaming tokens -> DOM patching and progressive rendering.

FastAPI example uses async generators and background tasks to pre-warm simple in-memory prefix cache for common prompts. Shows best-practice for graceful shutdown to flush streams. Includes pytest integration that asserts streaming frames arrive in order.

Go example focuses on context cancellation, http2 connection reuse, and minimizing allocations when forwarding tokens to clients. Includes a small retry wrapper that wraps net/http RoundTripper with backoff and jitter.

CLI examples show a common flag set (api-key, model, max-tokens, timeout, retry-policy) and a shared writeable-output pattern so streaming can be piped to other tools. Also demonstrates safe token logging practices (redact partial tokens).
Docs: each example will include an opinionated 'When to use' section and a short cost/latency checklist (batching, cache, quantization guidance).
Testing: add one e2e that runs the example server in CI using a local mock runtime (https://github.com/redwood-inference/mock-runtime) to validate streaming + retry behavior under transient errors.
